evidence.note: PlanShards rewritten to hash-bucket chunking; verified chunk boundaries always advance, hard-cut of an over-long line, injective HashFields preimages (internal/gitcontext/branchfiles.go:148), and stable shard/plan hashing.
appendRow: O_APPEND + flock + fsync, idempotent by id, id_conflict on head/workflow mismatch; defer order verified (unlock runs before Close).
Checked that the empty plan returned for a >16 MiB branch diff is intentional: DIFF_OVERSIZE is deliberately not in shardSatisfiableReasons, so shards are never expected to answer it.
CollectWithExcludes adds no implicit default excludes, so learnsource passing its own two-entry exclude list is not a regression of previously filtered paths.

Validation run locally: go build ./..., go vet and go test for contextprofile, fsm/record, learnsource, epicsource all pass; internal/fsm/record is 100.0% unit-covered, which is what tests/coverage.sh requires of internal/fsm/*.

Doc chunks verified against code: --shard-result / --cross-shard-result exist, and the fsm.md exit-code table matches machine.go:862-870 and cli/envelope.go exitFor (DONE(fixed|clean)=0, DONE(reviewed)/STOPPED/GATE_FAILED=1, NEEDS_INPUT=3).

findings.note: Documented shard-invalidation rule is narrower than the implementation. CLAUDE.md:91, docs/README.codex.md:87 and commands/review-task-done.md:33 state that editing a file invalidates only its own shard's result, but bucket width comes from bucketBits(needBuckets(total, budget)) over the whole branch diff, so a size change that crosses a power-of-two bucket boundary re-buckets every path and changes every shard id and hash; within one over-budget bucket the shards are packed sequentially over the sorted chunk list, so an edit that changes a file's chunk count also re-hashes the sibling split shards (id-2, id-3). Verified this fails safe: reviewmanifest freshness matches results by shardHash against current shards, so a stale result is ignored rather than counted, and the operator is only asked to re-review more shards than the docs promise, never fewer.

Torn-tail repair can discard a concurrently appended row. appendRow's own comment (record.go:182-188) records that runs.jsonl has a second writer, state.AppendJSONL, which takes no advisory lock; the append path is made safe against it by relying on O_APPEND atomicity, but the repair path is not: readRows re-reads the file, and f.Truncate(t.offset) then cuts the file back to the offset observed at read time, so a complete row appended by the unlocked writer in that window is lost (the torn fragment itself is quarantined first, the newer row is not). Narrow: requires a pre-existing torn tail plus a concurrent gate run, and the loss is one runs.jsonl row (attempt numbering), not audit state.

The new docs/metareview/fsm exclusion in learnsource has no test. internal/learnsource/source_test.go:157 (TestCollectExcludesShardResults) asserts only the docs/metareview/shards half of the same two-part exclude list, so a later edit could drop the fsm entries with the suite still green. Package coverage sits exactly on its floor (70.8), so the gap is not caught there either.

Dead API surface left by the shards.go rewrite: PlanShards no longer reads its profile parameter anywhere in the body (both callers, internal/taskdone/review.go:104 and internal/prready/review.go:106, still compute and pass a Profile), PlanSourceHash has no non-test caller and discards its Profile argument outright, and PlanShards no longer has any code path that returns a non-nil error while both callers still branch on one.

Row serializes contextPackPath and reviewLogPath unconditionally (no omitempty) but RowFor never sets them, so every FSM row in runs.jsonl carries empty strings in the two fields the review-gate writers populate with real paths. Consumers that read runs.jsonl generically will see an FSM run with no review log rather than a run that has none by design; either omitempty or a pointer to fsmRunDir would say that explicitly.
